summary.short: Bill adding Business and Professions Code Chapter 25 on automated decision systems used in consequential decisions such as employment and government benefits. Requires developers and deployers to perform impact assessments, give notice and explanations, and mitigate algorithmic discrimination risk; Civil Rights Department enforces via civil action.
summary.long: AB 2930 adds Business and Professions Code Chapter 25 on automated decision systems (ADS) used to make, or be a substantial factor in, consequential decisions about government benefits or services, government penalties, or employment (pay, promotion, hiring, termination, task allocation). Deployers must perform impact assessments before first deployment and annually; developers must do so before making a system available and give deployers results and documentation. Deployers must notify affected persons, explain the system and its outputs, allow an alternative selection process where feasible, and let persons correct personal data. Both must maintain a governance program against algorithmic discrimination, publish a summary policy, and keep assessments for five years. A system with an identified unmitigated risk of algorithmic discrimination may not be used or made available. Retaliation is unlawful. The Civil Rights Department may investigate and sue for injunctive and declaratory relief, and for algorithmic discrimination violations a $25,000 civil penalty per violation, after 45 days' notice and a cure opportunity. Cybersecurity technology is excluded. The registry lists the bill as failed.

relations.target_text: Government Code: Section 11546.45.5; Part 2.8 (commencing with Section 12900) of Division 3 of Title 2; Chapter 6 (commencing with Section 12940) of Part 2.8; Division 10 (commencing with Section 7920.000) of Title 1; Section 17556
relations.note: Section 11546.45.5 is incorporated into the definition of automated decision system (22756(c)(1)). Unlawful discrimination is defined by reference to Part 2.8 (22756(k)). Section 22756.12(a) preserves Chapter 6 remedies. Section 22756.7(b)(3) exempts disclosed impact assessments from the Public Records Act (Division 10). SEC. 3 cites Section 17556 on cost reimbursement.

relations.note: Section 51 is part of the unlawful discrimination definition (22756(k)) and is preserved by 22756.12(a). Sections 1798.140 and 56.05 define the information categories in impact assessment content (22756.1(b)(3), (d)(3)). Section 3426.1 defines trade secrets for the disclosure exemptions (22756.3(b), 22756.12(d)).

evidence.quote: any act that violates Section 51 of the Civil Code

notes: The document is the bill text only. It carries no version date and no legislative history, so the failed/dead status comes from registry metadata, not from the text. Operative provisions are in Section 1 (new Chapter 25); Sections 2 and 3 are a public-access finding and a cost statement. Drafting inconsistency: 22756.1(a)(2)(B) refers to 'an automated decision tool system', while the defined term is 'automated decision system' (22756(c)). The 55-employee exemption appears in both 22756.1(f) and 22756.4(c). Enforcement by the Civil Rights Department is in 22756.7 and 22756.9.
